title: How many hours of daylight does a city get each day?
description: A month's total hours of daylight in two cities are turned into hours per day by dividing by the days in the month. The video does this for June and December. Keeko thinks City one gets five hundred and sixty four hours a day.
teaching_notes: One idea: a monthly total is shared equally among the days of the month to give a daily average. Watch for students who read the month's total as the hours in one day.

source: Monthly hours of daylight in two cities: City 1 had 564 hours in June and 186 in December; City 2 had 276 in June and 468 in December; find the daylight per day
video_script.why: The child can find a mean by sharing a total, and now shares a monthly total among the days of the month.
video_script.substitution: The book's own monthly daylight hours for City 1 and City 2, for June and December.
video_script.anchor: Monthly hours of daylight. June (30 days): City 1 564, City 2 276. December (31 days): City 1 186, City 2 468.
video_script.wrong_answer: City one gets five hundred and sixty four hours a day
video_script.wrong_move: Reads the whole month's total as the daylight of one day, without dividing by the number of days.
video_script.payoff_line: In June, City one gets eighteen point eight hours a day, and City two gets nine point two.

final_answer.value: June: City 1 18.8, City 2 9.2 hours a day; December: City 1 6, City 2 about 15.1 hours a day
final_answer.spoken: June, City one eighteen point eight and City two nine point two hours a day; December, City one six and City two about fifteen point one hours a day

maths_rules: December has 31 days: City 1 186 / 31 = 6; City 2 468 / 31 = 15.096, about 15.1
check: 30 x 20 = 600 is a little more than 564; 30 x 9 = 270 is a little less than 276; 31 x 6 = 186; 31 x 15 = 465 is close to 468
City 1 is longest in June and City 2 is shortest in June
video_script.design: One idea: share the month's hours equally among its days. The four monthly totals sit in the anchor; on the board each total is shared into equal day boxes.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the daylight per day for each city, in June and in December.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, take June, which has thirty days.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>For City one, share five hundred and sixty four hours among thirty days.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>For City two, share two hundred and seventy six hours among thirty days.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, take December, which has thirty one days.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>City one shares one hundred and eighty six hours among thirty one days.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>City two shares four hundred and sixty eight hours among thirty one days.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, check with round numbers.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirty days of twenty hours make six hundred, a little more than five hundred and sixty four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Thirty days of nine hours make two hundred and seventy.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>That is a little less than two hundred and seventy six.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Thirty one days of six hours make one hundred and eighty six.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>Thirty one days of fifteen hours make four hundred and sixty five.
<bookmark mark='m7'/>That is close to four hundred and sixty eight.
